key_insight: Bigger pretrained segmentation models do not reliably deliver better cell and nucleus segmentation once energy use and model size are included, so sustainability-aware ranking can change model choice.
clinical_relevance: For biomedical image analysis teams, SAPI helps choose models that balance segmentation quality with compute cost, supporting more practical and environmentally responsible deployment.
method: Introduced the Sustainability-Aware Performance Index (SAPI) combining performance, energy, and model size.
Benchmarked 19 pretrained/foundation models on six CellBinDB datasets in zero-shot settings.
Evaluated 16 fine-tunable models with few-shot adaptation using frozen-encoder and full fine-tuning.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports software-based energy estimates for GPU, CPU, and RAM, and finds that SAPI rankings differ from performance-only rankings across models, datasets, and adaptation strategies.
watch_item: Energy and carbon estimates depend on the monitoring setup and deployment context, so SAPI should be used as a comparative decision aid rather than a universal score.
paper_title: Performance at What Cost? A Sustainability-Aware Performance Index for Cell and Nucleus Instance Segmentation
